evals.prompt: Design a landing page for a handmade pottery studio that sells weekend workshop seats. They have no brand yet.
evals.expected_output: Should propose a concrete subject, audience and primary job first, then make opinionated palette/typography/layout choices grounded in pottery craft (clay, kiln, hands), opening the hero with the most characteristic thing in that world — not a generic big-number headline.
assertions: Proposes a concrete subject, audience and primary job before designing
Grounds palette and typography choices in the pottery subject matter
Opens the hero with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world
Makes opinionated distinctive choices rather than templated defaults
Avoids the big-number-with-small-label default hero treatment unless justified

evals.prompt: Review my hero headline: 'Handcrafted magic for your home' with section labels in ALL CAPS above every block.
evals.expected_output: Should flag the single-accented-word headline treatment and the all-caps labels as generic generated-page tells, and suggest type-as-design-element alternatives with a clear type scale.
assertions: Flags accenting a single word in the headline as a generic tell
Flags all-caps labels above content as a generic tell
Suggests treating type itself as an active design element
Recommends one or two clearly distinct typefaces with a clear scale

evals.prompt: I want numbered markers 01/02/03 on my features section, fade-and-slide-up on every section, and hover transitions on all cards for our accounting software landing.
evals.expected_output: Should reject numbered markers because the features are not a sequence, reject scattered fade-and-slide-up entrances and per-card hovers as the generic default, and allow at most one orchestrated motion moment plus motion that answers user actions.
assertions: Rejects numbered markers because the content is not a sequence
Rejects fade-and-slide-up on every section as the generic default
Rejects hover transitions on every card as the generic default
Allows a single orchestrated motion moment at most
Keeps motion that answers a user action (opening, expanding, confirming)
